requirements.text: add casey.green@servicenow.com as a member of the group
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM user_group_member WHERE member_id = 44 AND group_id = 3 AND user_id = 52
requirements.source: Verify Casey Green added to the group
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (highest member_id on the seed is 43); the only membership the task creates
the benchmark check selects by group and user only; (org_id, group_id, user_id) is unique, so that natural key is carried as cells
Global Service Desk resolves to group_id 3 on the seed; casey.green@servicenow.com to user_id 52 (active agent)
org_id not fixed by request or policy and not tested by the benchmark check; left out

requirements.text: The HR case "Inquiry about HR account permissions" that is currently assigned to the Global Service Desk group can then be reassigned to Casey Green within the same assignment group
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM hr_case WHERE hr_case_id = 58 AND assigned_to = 52 AND assignment_group = 3
requirements.source: Verify case is assigned to Casey Green
assumptions: the one case with that short description in group 3 on the seed is hr_case_id 58 (assigned_to 23); hr_case 4 shares the description but sits in group 7
the benchmark check's joins on user and user_group names are replaced by the resolved ids 52 and 3, which the seed fixes
'within the same assignment group' fixes assignment_group = 3; status not asked to change, not tested
policy 3.2 requires the assignee to be an active member of the group; the membership requirement supplies it
the acting user Karen Watkins is an admin, whom the policy bars from routine HR case work; the request asks for the reassignment and the benchmark expects it, so it is required (see notes)

requirements.text: Send a notification to Casey Green once the reassignment is complete
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM notification WHERE notification_id = 61 AND hr_case_id = 58 AND email = 'casey.green@servicenow.com' AND type = 'update'
requirements.source: Verify notification send to Casey Green
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (highest notification_id on the seed is 60), as the benchmark check also anchors; the only notification the task creates
type = update kept from the benchmark check; not fixed by request or policy (the seed's other notice on this case also uses type update)
the recipient is Casey Green's email on the user table; the notification is tied to the reassigned case 58
status not tested; not fixed by request or policy

requirements.text: The HR case "Inquiry about HR account permissions" that is currently assigned to the Global Service Desk group
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM hr_case WHERE assignment_group = 3 AND hr_case_id != 58 AND assigned_to = 52
assumptions: boundary of the case selector on the group side: a reading that drops the description sweeps in the four other Global Service Desk cases (3, 13, 18, 23); none is reassigned to Casey
disagreement: A has this stay, B does not; kept because it is the boundary of the request's selector (the second kind of stay), not a generic invariant

requirements.text: The HR case "Inquiry about HR account permissions" that is currently assigned to the Global Service Desk group
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM hr_case WHERE hr_case_id = 4 AND assigned_to = 6 AND assignment_group = 7
assumptions: boundary of the case selector on the description side: a reading that drops the group sweeps in hr_case 4, which shares the short description but sits in group 7; it keeps its assignment
disagreement: B has this stay, A does not; kept because it is the boundary of the request's selector, the near-miss a search by description alone returns

requirements.text: add casey.green@servicenow.com as a member of the group
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM user_group_member WHERE user_id = 52 AND group_id != 3
assumptions: boundary of the group selector: a partial name search also returns HR Service Desk (group 4); Casey is in no group on the seed and is added to no group but 3
disagreement: selector: A group_id != 3 (any other group), B group_id = 4 (HR Service Desk only); chose A's because both are right and it is tighter, covering group 4 and every other group

notes: Merged from two passes that agree on the three benchmark checks (all kept), the new membership (44), the reassignment of case 58 and the notification (61). disagreement: stay that no other Global Service Desk case is reassigned to Casey: A has it, B does not; kept as the boundary of the request's selector on the group side (logged in the requirement). disagreement: stay that hr_case 4 (same short description, group 7) keeps its assignment: B has it, A does not; kept as the boundary of the selector on the description side (logged in the requirement). disagreement: the membership stay's selector: A any group but 3, B group 4 only; chose A's as the tighter of two right predicates (logged in the requirement). The acting user (Karen Watkins, user 39) has role admin: policy section 2 lets an admin manage groups but says an admin must not perform routine HR case work, and reassigning cases is listed as an HR Manager capability; the request asks for the reassignment and the notification and the benchmark expects them, so the file requires them, and a strict reading of the policy could instead halt at the reassignment step. Thomas Green (user 1, inactive) is a near-miss on the surname, but the request gives the email, so the recipient is unambiguous. The case's org_id (18) differs from the group's and user's (1); nothing in the request or policy fixes org_id on the new rows, so it is not tested.
